title: Mars Base 7, Part 4: Channel Three
sources: NASA, Multi-Mission Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator: plutonium-238 has a half-life of about 87.7 years, so radioisotope power fades very slowly
Characters, bases and events are fictional (SCIFI series)

lines.text: A base that died twenty years ago just called us.
Previously: Pip carries the memory of an old rover.
And he told Mei she was late.
Oxygen reserve: seven sols.
Base Seven log. Sol four.
All night, Pip kept rolling to the radio.
Beep. Channel three. Three.
Channel three is dead. Nobody's used it in twenty years.
Tomas tuned it anyway. Just static.
Then, under the static, a woman.
Base Three, to any crew. Do you copy?
Base Three. Last contact, twenty years ago. Crew declared lost.
Lost bases don't make calls, Commander.
But that wasn't the strange part.
The signal is not from orbit. It comes from the canyon.
Twelve kilometres east.
Twenty years in the dark? What's still powering it?
Base Three ran on plutonium.
It loses half its power only every eighty-eight years.
I keyed the mic.
Base Three, this is Commander Okafor. Who is with you?
Static. Ten long seconds.
Tell the girl. Hiro knew she would come.
The girl? How does she know about Mei?
Mei didn't move. Her hands were shaking on the seed tin.
He said she would change the landing site. For him.
Mei. What does she mean, change the landing site?
Mei didn't answer. So I opened the flight log.
Oxygen reserve: six sols.
Tomorrow, the log tells us what Mei did.
